author: __Talus__
body:
Age: 17

Timezone: GMT +10 (AEST)

Do you have access to TeamSpeak? Yes/No: Yes

Do you have access to Skype? Yes/No: Yes

Do you have access to a recording software? Yes/No: Yes 

 

CRITERIA 1: SELF REFLECTION/EVALUATION

 

Do you have any experience as a staff member on any servers?
I have a fair amount of experience in moderating Minecraft servers. I was a Helper on the Hypixel Network from April 2015 to October 2015, as well as previously being on the Avicus Staff team from December 2015 to January 2016, and again from March 2016 to August 2016. I also have experience being an Admin on some smaller servers that never took off.

 

What is your biggest weakness and how do you believe it will affect your moderating? What is your biggest strength and how would this affect your moderating?

My weakness that will affect my moderating is misjudgment. I can remember from my time as a Helper on Hypixel and a Moderator on Avicus that I have unintentionally banned or muted someone for something they may have done that was allowed that I was not aware of (false banning, accusations etc). It doesn't happen often but it always happens when I don't want it to. I'm working on increasing my hack detection skills to be a more useful member of the community. My biggest strength that will affect my moderating is interacting with people. I love talking to various members of the community, staff team and events teams on the various servers I have been staff on. I like talking to people and I find it incredibly rude if someone doesn't respond to me when I say "Hey" in Teamspeak or if I want to start a conversation in Slack. I really enjoy getting to know as many members of the community so I can build a good reputation and make fair judgments in various situations.

 

How do you believe you can help improve the Staff Team?
I believe I can improve the staff team by being a person that people can talk to if they need advice on how to deal with trouble makers, or even as some emotional support should they need it. I know this community is fairly fragile and I really want to be someone people can vent to and let me know about what's going on. I am also very polite when it comes to official matters and will step up when I need to, as well as consistently performing well as a Moderator in general. Finally, I enjoy a bit of banter on the side, so I can take a joke as well as being able to tell them. 

 

What qualities does a leader need to have in your opinion? Do you consider yourself to be a leader? Why?
To me, a leader has to be reliable, good at what they do and supportive. I believe I am a good leader that will make the necessary calls to ensure the task at hand is completed successfully and without any errors. I will also go out of my way to ensure my team are handling the situation well and assist if necessary. Since I am a Team Leader at my job in real life, the skills I have gained from that will greatly benefit my role as a potential moderator on the Avicus staff team.

 

What attributes distinguish yourself from other players that qualify you to be a moderator?
I believe that the thing that separates me from other potential mods is that I love dealing with the administrative side of the server. Of course moderators don't do much of that, but I thoroughly enjoy dealing with staff applications, ban appeals and reports on the server. It's something that I enjoy and I believe most people do not. For example, on my friend's server, I dealt with all the staff applications, ban appeals and ban requests, as well as dealing with the players on the server. To me, I found this more fun than say, coding the server or building. I believe this separates me from other applicants. 

 

What skills do you believe you should have when interacting with the community? Do you believe you have these skills?

I believe that the necessary skills that someone must possess to interact with the community are that they must be tough skinned, open, friendly and unbiased. I believe I have these skills as I can tell from experience. I have been staffing on servers big and small for the past 4 years and I have developed a proper ideology that works for me when it comes to being a model staff member. This is that I must be unbiased, friendly and tough skinned, since there are some toxic people out there and being tough skinned and friendly are both needed to make an unbiased decision on how to deal with the player, whether I know them or not. On bigger networks such as Avicus, it is also essential you are as open as you can be so people don't complain about the staff team being secretive.

 

How much time can you commit to being a staff member (Rough Idea)? 

I can dedicate at least 2 hours per day and more on the weekends, up to 6 or 7 depending on when I'm working and when school is.

 

CRITERIA 2: GENERAL SITUATIONS

 

You are currently undergoing your junior moderator trial. A ban evader is online and he is constantly ban evading and hacking. You are the only one online and the only one who is able to be online. What would you do?

First of all, I would get an admin or senior moderator to check the person's history (accounts banned, ip etc). After that, I would record a couple of instances of the person hacking to have proof in case they decide to appeal. After that, I would ask a Moderator to assist in banning the person while I record them and contact the senior or admin.

 

Another staff member is constantly joining and harassing other people on Teamspeak in their team channel. The staff member is also referee and has physical permissions to be in that channel. However the leaders do not want this staff member in there and they have asked him to leave multiple times. What would you do?

I would first talk to the team leader and see what they have to say about what they've been doing. After that I would attempt to talk to the offending staff member to see why they were doing it and ask if they can stop doing what they're doing. Whether they stop or not, I would ultimately report it to a seinor and request them to review the staff member and their actions.

 

 

A player appeals a punishment you gave them. You realise that the evidence file is corrupted and therefore there is no physical evidence. You know however this person did indeed break the rules, what would you do?

First of all, I would find their punishment history and attempt to find some kind of recent proof that they should not be unbanned. After that, I would consult a couple of moderators to see if they know anything about the player and their history. Finally, if I cannot find anymore evidence, I would ask a senior mod to assist me in dealing with the player. 

 

You are in an Avicus team. One of your teammates is also an Avicus Staff member. One day in your team discord the team member/staff member posts a screenshot of a thread that only staff members can see. The content in the screenshot isn’t very important/confident but only staff members could see it on the forums. If anything, what would you do?

I would just ask the team member on the quiet why they shared the screenshot knowing that any form of leaking is punishable. After that, I would report it to a senior on the downlow about what the staff member had done.

 

One day the Senior Staff team makes a decision you do not agree with. You do not know all the details of the decision or the circumstances in which they were made and you were simply told by another staff member. However you do not like the decision based from what you know. What would you do?

I would ask one of the senior staff team for more information on the decision so I can make a better judgement on the situation than just on what another moderator told me. I believe information is key and if I came at the team aggressively then it might make a bad situation worse, plus I would look like a fool. 

 

 

CRITERIA 3: OTHER

NOTE: This is a new criteria and these questions are less to do with right/wrong answer and more to do with us getting to know you. Please answer these honestly. There is no right or wrong answer.

 

 

What would getting moderator on Avicus mean to you?

Becoming moderator on Avicus again would mean a lot to me. I did enjoy my last run on the team and my demotion was because of a couple of snide comments on slack and teamspeak power abuse. I will be a much better moderator this time round and I really want to see Avicus grow. I do like the community and would love to contribute more to it than just being a lurker on the forums.

 

How passionate are you about Avicus? What does Avicus mean to you?

I really love how unique and close-knit the community of Avicus is. Although there are a couple of troublemakers, the community is definitely the thing that attracts me most. The community is small enough for most people to know everyone but big enough to be a reputable network.

 

Do you speak any other languages than English?

 I know basic conversational Japanese.

 

Do you have anything else to add to your application?

N/A


Kind regards,

iCatNoir (formerly KenyaNot)
